top.title: Inside the Numbers: Texas found a recipe for success
top.description: AUSTIN, TX - NOVEMBER 21: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning #16 runs with the ball as Arkansas Razorbacks defensive back Shelton Lewis #2 pursues during the SEC football game between Texas Longhorns and Arkansas Razorbacks on November 21, 2026, at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The No. 5 Texas Longhorns looked like flat track bully for the second time in three weeks, dominating the Arkansas Razorbacks in the home finale on Saturday at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Arch Manning was dealing, the offense was humming, and the defense was once again dominant, imposing their will on Arkansas from wire to wire. Now, the Longhorns are playing for style points, trying to secure their place in the postseason hierarchy. Arch Manning: 21-25, 287 yards, 2 TD Following Arch Manning is enough to give you whiplash. After having the worst games of his career, he turned in one of the best — thanks in large part to the game plan. After going away from the short game against LSU, much to the detriment of the offense, the Longhorns leaned back into it against Arkansas and feasted. Manning was a perfect 10-of-10 on passing attempts at or behind the line of scrimmage, averaging 10.7 yards per attempt at that range . If you add in anything shorter than five yards, 141 (49 percent) of his passing yardage in the game came in the short game. At one point, Manning completed nine consecutive passes, the longest streak of the season, six of them going for either a first down or a touchdown. That streak includes four of the Texas explosive passing plays on it, including Emmett Mosley V’s 17-yard touchdown to end the first half. That was one of Mosley’s eight receptions for 106 yards on the day, his first 100-yard game as a Longhorn. Third downs: 6-11 (54.5 percent) The Texas offense has been rightfully criticized for its third-down performance this year, sitting near the bottom of the conference in third-down conversions, but they bucked that trend on Saturday. Converting six of 11 gives them their best conversion percentage since the start of conference play, averaging an abysmal 34.6 percent since they started SEC games in September. A big part of their success was how they set themselves up for third and short, which is obviously the optimal outcome for an offense. They averaged 5.3 yards on an average distance of 4.9 yards, needing to gain four or fewer yards on six of their 11 attempts. First-down success set Texas up for manageable third downs or avoided them entirely, averaging 9.1 yards per play, including 12.6 yards per attempt for Arch Manning. Texas scored three first-down touchdowns — a 21-yard pass to tight end Emaree Winston, a one-yard rush by Michael Terry set up by a 30-yard first-down pass to Raleek Brown, and a fourth-quarter exclamation point by Derrek Cooper. (Photo by Rebecca Villagracia/Getty Images) Louisville and Lincoln Kienholz picked up an emphatic victory on Saturday over Pittsburgh. Kienholz threw five touchdowns, and the Cardinals won 42-10. It was a fun day to be Louisville. That is, until the postgame press conference when Kienholz was asked about his future. In modern college football, players — especially quarterbacks — get asked about what they’re doing next as if they’re a free agent. They sort of are. Kienholz had just arrived at Louisville this season after transferring from Ohio State, so he’s not a stranger to the transfer portal. With one week remaining in the regular season, Kienholz was asked the tough question on Saturday. The way he handled it has some Louisville fans worried. Lincoln Kienholz Quote on Future Getty LOUISVILLE, KENTUCKY – NOVEMBER 21: Lincoln Kienholz #3 of the Louisville Cardinals runs with the ball while defended by Jeremiah Marcelin #32 of the Pittsburgh Panthers in the first quarter at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Louisville, Kentucky. It’s more of just those guys just focused on those things so I can focus on football.” On the one hand, that’s a fair answer. Kienholz doesn’t owe anyone a deeper explanation than that right now. On the other hand, it does sound like a guy who isn’t exactly committing himself to Louisville’s 2027 roster. It’d be tough for Louisville to lose Kienholz, but if he chooses to leave, he’d have plenty of interested teams chasing after him in the portal. top.title: Chiefs Make Rare Patrick Mahomes Decision Days Before Bills Game
top.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 22: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs reacts against the Arizona Cardinals during the third quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs’ blowout against the Arizona Cardinals was so lopsided that CBS switched to another game. With the Chiefs facing the Buffalo Bills in a matter of days, head coach Andy Reid opted to take some precaution with Patrick Mahomes. With the Chiefs leading the Cardinals 34-7 in the fourth quarter, Reid decided to rest Mahomes and inserted Justin Fields as the team’s quarterback to close out the game. It is worth noting that Mahomes is just two weeks removed from sustaining what looked to be a scary elbow injury. Mahomes has been able to play through the injury without missing time. With the game out of reach, Reid opted not to risk Mahomes sustaining further injury. Here’s what you need to know about the latest Chiefs news. The Chiefs Turned to Justin Fields as Patrick Mahomes Continues to Recover From Elbow Injury Kansas City traded for Fields during the offseason as insurance behind Mahomes as the quarterback was recovering from a season-ending ACL injury at the time of the deal. Reid has been outspoken about his trust in Fields. “I like his game,” Reid said regarding Fields during a March media session, per Pro Football Talk. “He can do the drop back game, he can do the movement stuff, play-action — whether it’s a naked or a sprint-out game. “He has that whole package that he can do. He understands the screen game, understands how to set it up. He obviously — he’s going to be one of the better athletes on the field when he’s out there,” Reid continued. “He’s fast, big, likes to play the game. So, I mean, all the stuff I like.” Chiefs vs. Bills: Kansas City Is a 3-Point Underdog Against Buffalo in NFL Odds for Thanksgiving Game The Chiefs will travel to Buffalo for a holiday matchup against the Bills. It appears as though Mahomes and the Chiefs will enter Thanksgiving as the underdog. Ahead of Week 11, the Bills were a 3-point favorite against the Chiefs in the early lookahead line. top.title: JJ Spaun Makes History With Stunning Eight-Shot Victory at Dunlop Phoenix
top.description: Jun 15, 2025; Oakmont, Pennsylvania, USA; JJ Spaun celebrates with the championship trophy after winning the 125th U.S. Open golf tournament. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Orlando Fuller JJ Spaun has claimed his third victory of the year after winning the Dunlop Phoenix Tournament in Japan by eight shots. The 36-year-old American finished at 16-under 264 at Phoenix Country Club in Miyazaki, with Yusaku Hosono finishing second. Spaun had not played since winning the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth on September 20 . He returned to competition after more than two months away and produced another impressive performance to win his second consecutive event. The 2025 U.S. Open champion opened with a six-under 66 before carding a 70 in the second round. However, his performance over the weekend put him well clear of the rest of the field and secured the biggest winning margin of his season. Spaun Takes Control With 62 in Third Round Spaun made his move in the third round, shooting an eight-under 62 on the par-70 course. His round included seven birdies and an eagle, giving him a commanding lead heading into Sunday’s final round. He then followed it with another strong performance, making five birdies to shoot a four-under 66. That took him to 16 under for the tournament and gave him an eight-shot advantage over Hosono. The victory came at an event that has welcomed several major names in golf over the years. Johnny Miller, Seve Ballesteros, Tom Watson, Ernie Els and David Duval have all won the Dunlop Phoenix. Tiger Woods also claimed the title in 2004 and 2005, while Brooks Koepka won consecutive editions in 2016 and 2017. Spaun has now added his name to that list after dominating the tournament across the final two rounds. Spaun Adds Dunlop Phoenix Title to Successful 2026 Season Spaun’s latest victory follows his win at the BMW PGA Championship, where he finished two shots clear of Rory McIlroy, Adam Scott and Aaron Rai. He produced a final-round 67 at Wentworth to claim the title after missing out on a place in the U.S. Presidents Cup team. The American had been disappointed with his omission from Brandt Snedeker’s team for the competition at Medinah. He had expected to be part of the team before the captain selected Jacob Bridgeman and Jackson Koivun as his final two picks. Spaun instead travelled to Wentworth and won the tournament in his first appearance at the DP World Tour event. He has now followed that result with another title after returning from his two-month break. His other victory this year came at the PGA Tour’s Valero Texas Open in April, the week before the Masters. The Dunlop Phoenix win gives him three titles in 2026 and continues a strong run for the world No. 13. Other notable players in Japan included Ryo Ishikawa, who finished tied for fourth, while former LIV Golf player and NCAA champion Michael La Sasso finished tied for 11th. top.title: ‘That offense is pathetic’: Urban Meyer says Michigan offense ‘stinks’ ahead of Ohio State showdown
top.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Ohio State Buckeyes and Michigan Wolverines are both limping into this year’s edition of The Game, with each program closing out a disappointing regular season and each head coach facing questions about his future. Ohio State’s College Football Playoff hopes ended with a loss at Nebraska on Saturday, and while Michigan pulled off a stunning upset of No. 4 UCLA later that night, the win only got the Wolverines to 6-5. Now, former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer has offered his prediction for next Saturday’s matchup in Columbus. And while Meyer had plenty of praise for Michigan’s defense, he called the Wolverines’ offense “pathetic” and said he expects a low-scoring game. Disappointing Seasons For Both Ohio State’s season has fallen apart over the last month. The Buckeyes started 6-1, but quarterback Julian Sayin suffered an arm injury late in a 19-15 win over Indiana, and they’ve since lost to USC, Oregon, and now Nebraska with freshman Luke Fahey under center. Saturday’s 31-28 loss in Lincoln dropped Ohio State to 7-4 and officially knocked the Buckeyes out of playoff contention. Needless to say, the criticism of Ryan Day has never been louder. Michigan’s season hasn’t gone any better under first-year head coach Kyle Whittingham. The Wolverines have flip-flopped between Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr at quarterback, and they entered Saturday ranked 131st in the country in scoring at 18.3 points per game. But Michigan’s defense kept the Wolverines in it against UCLA, and they won 18-16 in triple overtime when Underwood threw a 2-point conversion pass to Jalen Hoffman. The win handed the Bruins their first loss of the season and made Michigan bowl-eligible. Still, one upset isn’t likely to change much for Whittingham, whose future at Michigan is expected to be decided after the season. Neither team is exactly making a strong case for this year’s game, either. Before Michigan’s win, Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy, who is a longtime Michigan fan, called it the “worst big game” in the history of the rivalry and said both programs need an embarrassing loss so they can fire their coaches. ‘Their offense stinks’ Speaking on stage at a recent event, Meyer said Michigan’s defense deserves a lot of credit for how the Wolverines have stayed competitive this season, in a clip shared by Eleven Warriors . “I think the Wolverine defense is legit, legit, because that offense is pathetic up there. It’s the worst offense in college football, yet they’re in almost all the games. And we covered them on Big Noon a bunch. And their defense, what they did to UCLA, was absolutely phenomenal,” Meyer said. He then turned to his former team, noting that the Buckeyes haven’t been consistent on either side of the ball. “Our defense has been up and down a little bit, but their offense stinks. Our offense has been up and down a little bit, and now we’re down to our backup quarterback. So I see this being a very low-scoring game.

top.title: Great escape? ESPN loses 7 million pay-TV homes following UFC departure
top.description: BRISTOL, CONNECTICUT - NOVEMBER 03: A logo sign at the entrance to the ESPN headquarters on November 03, 2024 in Bristol, Connecticut. (Photo by Kirby Lee/Getty Images) | Getty Images ESPN’s traditional television footprint continues to shrink — and Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) may have picked an ideal time to find a new broadcast partner . ESPN and ESPN2 are each available in approximately 54 million pay-TV homes, according to Disney’s latest annual filing . That represents a loss of seven million subscribers from Sept. 2025, when both networks reportedly reached roughly 61 million homes. At its peak in 2011, ESPN was available in approximately 100 million households. At ESPN’s reported $9.42 monthly carriage fee, New York Post estimates the seven-million-home decline represents more than $791 million in annualized carriage-fee value. However, that figure does not account for rate increases or ESPN’s growing direct-to-consumer business. Those shrinking subscriber totals have not stopped ESPN from opening its wallet for its biggest personalities. Stephen A. Smith signed a five-year contract reportedly worth approximately $100 million in 2025 — roughly $20 million annually. ESPN also agreed to pay approximately $85 million over five years to license The Pat McAfee Show , averaging $17 million per year. That McAfee figure covers the entire program and its production costs, not simply his salary. Together, the deals represent approximately $185 million in reported commitments while ESPN and ESPN2 have lost 12 million pay-TV homes since 2024, falling from 66 million to 54 million. Who doesn’t love Smith and McAfee, right? Can you feel my sarcasm? The timing is certainly interesting for fight fans. After seven years with ESPN, UFC moved its entire United States schedule to Paramount+ at the beginning of 2026. Paramount paid $7.7 billion for the seven-year agreement , averaging $1.1 billion annually — more than double the reported value of UFC’s previous ESPN deal. The move also eliminated UFC’s expensive pay-per-view model . Every numbered event and “Fight Night” card is now included with a Paramount+ subscription, while select major events are simulcast on CBS. To be clear, UFC’s departure did not cause ESPN to lose seven million pay-TV homes. The figures also measure ESPN and ESPN2 distribution, not subscriptions to ESPN’s standalone streaming service. Nevertheless, the decline illustrates the rapidly changing sports-media business UFC left behind. ESPN still controls a massive collection of valuable sports rights — and recently landed WWE premium live events — but its traditional cable reach is now nearly half what it was 15 years ago. Did UFC get out at exactly the right time ?

nigeria.title: Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29
nigeria.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. Governor Douye Diri disclosed this during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established as efforts were still ongoing to recover the affected vessel. ﻿ He, however, said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat. The governor described the incident as avoidable, alleging that the boat was not fit for river travel and had operated from an unauthorised loading point. He said the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of the survivors. Diri thanked President Tinubu for the concern shown by the Presidency since the incident occurred, particularly the Vice President’s visit to the state. He used the occasion to appeal for Federal Government support for the construction of more roads across Bayelsa, noting that improved road access would reduce the dependence of some communities on water transportation. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, adding that the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. The boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways, according to a preliminary police report. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings. President Bola Tinubu expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. nigeria.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos Is The Big Deal To Me, Says Tinubu
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has described Lagos State as crucial ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise voters and ensure a higher turnout in the state. Tinubu spoke on Sunday during a prayer session at the hall of the Yoruba Tennis Club in Lagos, where he urged them not to generate the maximum win. “The challenge of today is much easier than that of yesterday. But we cannot take it for granted. You must knock on your neighbour’s door. “Tell them to get, collect their PVC,” he said. The President also urged the attendees at the prayer session that collecting the Permanent Voter Card (PVC) was essential to exercising their democratic rights. “If you are here and you don’t have PVC, you are just here for amala and ewedu,” he told those present jokingly. “If you have PVC, you have the power of January 16th and February 6. And that’s what I want to ask you to exercise. ”To me, Lagos is the big deal. How can you have seven million registered voters and produce 100,000-200,000 votes? That’s failure. “Even if you win, and say, ‘A win is a win,’ no. You have to generate the maximum,” he added. ﻿ Tinubu lost the state to Peter Obi , who was then the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, despite the President’s longstanding political influence in the commercial capital where he served as governor from 1999 to 2007. According to results announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Obi polled 582,454 votes to defeat Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes in the February 25, 2023 presidential election. The Peoples Democratic Party’s candidate in the election, Atiku Abubakar, came third with 75,750 votes, while Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party scored 8,442 votes. The results showed that although Tinubu won 11 of Lagos State’s 20 local government areas, Obi secured the overall victory, winning nine local government areas, including Alimosho, Ojo and Oshodi-Isolo. Lagos had 6,214,970 PVCs collected ahead of the 2023 election, the highest number recorded by any state in the country. However, only 1,335,729 votes were cast in the state, comprising 1,271,451 valid votes and 64,278 rejected ballots. Tinubu is seeking to consolidate his political support in the state as he prepares for another presidential contest in 2027, with opposition candidates, including Obi and Atiku, also in the race. nigeria.title: ‘We need to turn that anger into energy’ – Pochettino reacts to Man Utd’s 4-0 loss
nigeria.description: Mauricio Pochettino said Manchester United must harness the pain from a 4-0 thrashing by Liverpool on Sunday into positive change despite feeling aggrieved by Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute red card. Pochettino’s reign got off to a nightmare start when Yoro was controversially sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak. United never recovered as Liverpool instantly took advantage when Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home the resulting free-kick. Defeat leaves United still second bottom of the Premier League and at risk of relegation from the English top flight for the first time since 1974. “It’s so painful, we feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game,” said Pochettino. “We need to accept the reality and we need to be responsible. We need to be united, we need to be all together and I think we feel disappointed because it’s clear that after eight minutes, I think, the plan was in the bin.” Isak had taken a heavy touch and the ball appeared to be running through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens before contact was made by Yoro. “I’m not going to change what happened and being respectful is always important,” added Pochettino. “At the same time I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card.” – ‘Changes the game completely’ – A repeat of United’s 7-0 thrashing at Anfield three years ago appeared on the cards when Florian Wirtz doubled Liverpool’s lead inside 13 minutes. However, Pochettino’s introduction of Harry Maguire and switch to a back five helped stem the bleeding until teenager Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz rounded off the rout in the second half. “It hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation,” said United captain Bruno Fernandes, who raged against the decision to dismiss Yoro. “There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game,” added the Portuguese international. “It’s not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely.” Victory lifts Liverpool up to fourth in the table and within seven points of leaders Arsenal. Andoni Iraola savoured the adulation coming his way at full-time and believes his side should have run up an even bigger margin of victory. Isak and Bradley Barcola were guilty of wasting a number of big chances either side of half-time. “It’s difficult to enjoy in the Premier League, normally you suffer even if you win, but I think we could celebrate at half-time and enjoy it a little bit,” said Iraola. “We have missed some clear chances today. nigeria.title: CJN tasks lawyers to embrace scholarship
nigeria.description: …Commends Pinheiro’s 6 law books By Innocent Anaba LAGOS—THE Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, has commended the contributions of Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, to legal scholarship and professional development, describing six publications presented in his honour as valuable resources that will enrich Nigerian jurisprudence and strengthen the intellectual foundation of the legal profession. Kekere-Ekun, who spoke, weekend, while chairing the public presentation of the books in Lagos, said the publications reflected an impressive combination of legal scholarship, practical experience and engagement with contemporary developments in the administration of justice. She noted that the collection, comprising four books authored by Pinheiro and two compilations produced in his honour, addressed significant areas of legal practice, including litigation, arbitration, insolvency, criminal law, technology and contemporary jurisprudence. According to her, the publications were not merely a collection of books assembled to commemorate an accomplished legal practitioner but works that sought to make legal knowledge more accessible and useful to those responsible for applying, interpreting and developing the law. The CJN said: “Taken together, the works reflect an engagement with important areas of legal practice and scholarship, as well as an attempt to preserve the experiences and contributions of a distinguished member of our profession.” Kekere-Ekun described ‘Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk’ as particularly significant because it offered a personal account of the experiences, encounters, challenges and defining moments that had shaped Pinheiro’s career spanning close to four decades at the Bar. She observed that memoirs of this nature were valuable because they preserved aspects of professional life that might never find their way into law reports or formal institutional records. Such accounts, she said, enabled younger practitioners to appreciate the human experiences behind professional milestones, including the uncertainties, disappointments and perseverance that often accompanied a successful legal career. The CJN also highlighted the importance of the two publications on arbitration and insolvency, particularly against the background of Nigeria’s increasingly sophisticated business environment and the need for effective legal responses to commercial transactions. , financial distress and dispute resolution. Teenager Rio Ngumoha rounded off a stunning individual with Liverpool’s third before Victor Munoz completed the rout. Defeat leaves United still rooted second bottom of the Premier League and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories. Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title. Pochettino answered United’s call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils’ first 10 league games in charge. The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans. Pochettino’s bold team selection backfired with the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game’s decisive moment. De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal. The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card. Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box. Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar. Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran centre-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding. United lost 7-0 at Anfield three years ago and a switch to a back five helped avoid similar damage, albeit with the help of some wayward Liverpool finishing. Maguire made a brilliant block to deny Isak a third goal just before half-time. Bradley Barcola and Isak were guilty of wasting huge chances early in the second half. But Barcola’s blistering pace created Liverpool’s third just after the hour mark. The French international destroyed Lisandro Martinez for pace before picking out Ngumoha to slot home. Wirtz rounded off one of his best Liverpool displays since a £100 million move from Bayer Leverkusen last year with the assist for Munoz to crash home the fourth goal eight minutes from time. Liverpool fans rejoiced in their rivals’ pain with chants of “you are going down”. United have not been relegated since 1974 but find themselves in a battle for survival despite still enjoying one of the biggest revenues in world football. entertainment.title: Elizabeth Agboola: Your Next Flight From Nigeria Could Be Two Holidays in One. Here’s How
entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. Turkish Airlines: Turn Istanbul Into Part of Your Holiday Turkish Airlines operates a Stopover in Istanbul programme for eligible international passengers connecting through Istanbul Airport. For visa purposes, Nigerians do not qualify, but with a valid Turkish visa you would be able to qualify for some of the perks. Qualifying travellers with connections of at least 20 hours and up to seven days may receive complimentary hotel accommodation. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The No. 5 Texas Longhorns looked like flat track bully for the second time in three weeks, dominating the Arkansas Razorbacks in the home finale on Saturday at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Arch Manning was dealing, the offense was humming, and the defense was once again dominant, imposing their will on Arkansas from wire to wire. Now, the Longhorns are playing for style points, trying to secure their place in the postseason hierarchy. Arch Manning: 21-25, 287 yards, 2 TD Following Arch Manning is enough to give you whiplash. After having the worst games of his career, he turned in one of the best — thanks in large part to the game plan. After going away from the short game against LSU, much to the detriment of the offense, the Longhorns leaned back into it against Arkansas and feasted. Manning was a perfect 10-of-10 on passing attempts at or behind the line of scrimmage, averaging 10.7 yards per attempt at that range . If you add in anything shorter than five yards, 141 (49 percent) of his passing yardage in the game came in the short game. At one point, Manning completed nine consecutive passes, the longest streak of the season, six of them going for either a first down or a touchdown. That streak includes four of the Texas explosive passing plays on it, including Emmett Mosley V’s 17-yard touchdown to end the first half. That was one of Mosley’s eight receptions for 106 yards on the day, his first 100-yard game as a Longhorn. Third downs: 6-11 (54.5 percent) The Texas offense has been rightfully criticized for its third-down performance this year, sitting near the bottom of the conference in third-down conversions, but they bucked that trend on Saturday. Converting six of 11 gives them their best conversion percentage since the start of conference play, averaging an abysmal 34.6 percent since they started SEC games in September. A big part of their success was how they set themselves up for third and short, which is obviously the optimal outcome for an offense. They averaged 5.3 yards on an average distance of 4.9 yards, needing to gain four or fewer yards on six of their 11 attempts. The 36-year-old American finished at 16-under 264 at Phoenix Country Club in Miyazaki, with Yusaku Hosono finishing second. The 2025 U.S. Open champion opened with a six-under 66 before carding a 70 in the second round. sports.title: ‘That offense is pathetic’: Urban Meyer says Michigan offense ‘stinks’ ahead of Ohio State showdown
sports.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Ohio State Buckeyes and Michigan Wolverines are both limping into this year’s edition of The Game, with each program closing out a disappointing regular season and each head coach facing questions about his future. Ohio State’s College Football Playoff hopes ended with a loss at Nebraska on Saturday, and while Michigan pulled off a stunning upset of No. 4 UCLA later that night, the win only got the Wolverines to 6-5. Now, former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer has offered his prediction for next Saturday’s matchup in Columbus. And while Meyer had plenty of praise for Michigan’s defense, he called the Wolverines’ offense “pathetic” and said he expects a low-scoring game. Disappointing Seasons For Both Ohio State’s season has fallen apart over the last month. The Buckeyes started 6-1, but quarterback Julian Sayin suffered an arm injury late in a 19-15 win over Indiana, and they’ve since lost to USC, Oregon, and now Nebraska with freshman Luke Fahey under center. Saturday’s 31-28 loss in Lincoln dropped Ohio State to 7-4 and officially knocked the Buckeyes out of playoff contention. Needless to say, the criticism of Ryan Day has never been louder. Michigan’s season hasn’t gone any better under first-year head coach Kyle Whittingham. The Wolverines have flip-flopped between Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr at quarterback, and they entered Saturday ranked 131st in the country in scoring at 18.3 points per game. But Michigan’s defense kept the Wolverines in it against UCLA, and they won 18-16 in triple overtime when Underwood threw a 2-point conversion pass to Jalen Hoffman. The win handed the Bruins their first loss of the season and made Michigan bowl-eligible. Still, one upset isn’t likely to change much for Whittingham, whose future at Michigan is expected to be decided after the season. Neither team is exactly making a strong case for this year’s game, either. Before Michigan’s win, Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy, who is a longtime Michigan fan, called it the “worst big game” in the history of the rivalry and said both programs need an embarrassing loss so they can fire their coaches. ‘Their offense stinks’ Speaking on stage at a recent event, Meyer said Michigan’s defense deserves a lot of credit for how the Wolverines have stayed competitive this season, in a clip shared by Eleven Warriors . “I think the Wolverine defense is legit, legit, because that offense is pathetic up there. It’s the worst offense in college football, yet they’re in almost all the games. And we covered them on Big Noon a bunch. And their defense, what they did to UCLA, was absolutely phenomenal,” Meyer said. He then turned to his former team, noting that the Buckeyes haven’t been consistent on either side of the ball. “Our defense has been up and down a little bit, but their offense stinks. sports.title: Kerby Joseph Takes Shot at Baker Mayfield Following Lions Victory
sports.description: Kerby Joseph waited 406 days to return to the football field, and apparently, he was hoping Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield would give him a welcome-back present. Unfortunately for Joseph, Mayfield wasn’t interested in cooperating. Following the Detroit Lions’ 31-21 victory over Tampa Bay on Sunday afternoon at Ford Field, Joseph had some fun with reporters when asked whether his long-awaited return went better than expected. “Nah, man, I need a pick, man. I need a pick,” Joseph said, according to Kory Woods of MLive. “It’s all right. I ain’t get it. They don’t want to throw the ball down there. They scared. Baker, it’s all right. Honestly, I’m just happy we got the dub. It’s not all about me, man. It’s about the team. So we get this dub, man, I’m fine. I still want that pick, but they got to throw it deep.” Well, welcome back, Kerby! Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph looks on during warmups ahead of the New Orleans Saints game at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Kerby Joseph Brings Confidence Back to Lions Secondary Joseph was making his first appearance since October 2025 after battling a lingering knee injury that kept him sidelined for more than a year. Despite serious questions surrounding his recovery , the All-Pro safety finally returned to action Sunday. According to the MLive report, Joseph played 46 defensive snaps and recorded two solo tackles. He didn’t come away with the interception he wanted, but his return provided a welcome boost for a Detroit defense dealing with several significant injuries. Mayfield finished with 187 passing yards and two touchdowns, but the Lions limited Tampa Bay’s offense when it mattered most. After previously firing back at critics who doubted his recovery , he was simply thrilled to be back on the field helping his teammates win. But make no mistake about it. Joseph still wants that interception, and judging by his comments about Mayfield, his confidence certainly hasn’t gone anywhere.

sports.title: Great escape? ESPN loses 7 million pay-TV homes following UFC departure
sports.description: BRISTOL, CONNECTICUT - NOVEMBER 03: A logo sign at the entrance to the ESPN headquarters on November 03, 2024 in Bristol, Connecticut. (Photo by Kirby Lee/Getty Images) | Getty Images ESPN’s traditional television footprint continues to shrink — and Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) may have picked an ideal time to find a new broadcast partner . ESPN and ESPN2 are each available in approximately 54 million pay-TV homes, according to Disney’s latest annual filing . That represents a loss of seven million subscribers from Sept. 2025, when both networks reportedly reached roughly 61 million homes. At its peak in 2011, ESPN was available in approximately 100 million households. At ESPN’s reported $9.42 monthly carriage fee, New York Post estimates the seven-million-home decline represents more than $791 million in annualized carriage-fee value. However, that figure does not account for rate increases or ESPN’s growing direct-to-consumer business. Those shrinking subscriber totals have not stopped ESPN from opening its wallet for its biggest personalities. Stephen A. Smith signed a five-year contract reportedly worth approximately $100 million in 2025 — roughly $20 million annually. ESPN also agreed to pay approximately $85 million over five years to license The Pat McAfee Show , averaging $17 million per year. That McAfee figure covers the entire program and its production costs, not simply his salary. Together, the deals represent approximately $185 million in reported commitments while ESPN and ESPN2 have lost 12 million pay-TV homes since 2024, falling from 66 million to 54 million. Who doesn’t love Smith and McAfee, right? Can you feel my sarcasm? The timing is certainly interesting for fight fans. After seven years with ESPN, UFC moved its entire United States schedule to Paramount+ at the beginning of 2026. Paramount paid $7.7 billion for the seven-year agreement , averaging $1.1 billion annually — more than double the reported value of UFC’s previous ESPN deal. The move also eliminated UFC’s expensive pay-per-view model . Every numbered event and “Fight Night” card is now included with a Paramount+ subscription, while select major events are simulcast on CBS. To be clear, UFC’s departure did not cause ESPN to lose seven million pay-TV homes. The figures also measure ESPN and ESPN2 distribution, not subscriptions to ESPN’s standalone streaming service. Nevertheless, the decline illustrates the rapidly changing sports-media business UFC left behind. ESPN still controls a massive collection of valuable sports rights — and recently landed WWE premium live events — but its traditional cable reach is now nearly half what it was 15 years ago. Did UFC get out at exactly the right time ?

technology.title: As cars go digital, US consumers pay an extra $12 billion a year for repairs
technology.description: The computerization of cars comes at a price to US consumers, according to the Public Interest Research Group (PIRG), which says that software fees and other charges faced by mechanics push up garage costs. An investigation by the non-profit consumer group estimates that car repair costs for Americans have been inflated by $12 billion each year, as vehicles integrate more computerized functions. Its report, Closing Shop , is available online. To find a failed sensor, release an electronic parking brake, or perform diagnostics, a technician has to first connect a laptop or tablet to the vehicle. To so this, the repair shop has to have the right software tools, and that means paying the vehicle manufacturer subscription charges and other fees, in order to get the information they need to complete the job. If smaller independent repair shops can’t afford all the necessary software or subscriptions, they may be forced to steer customers to authorized dealerships for some fixes – about one in five jobs – and this allows the latter to charge more. PIRG claims that drivers pay for this through their insurance premiums, even if they never need to get their car fixed, because higher repair costs mean higher insurance claims. It says the price of auto insurance has risen three times as fast as the rest of the US economy since 2012. Even if mechanics do choose to pay for the software, they spend an estimated collective 83 million hours a year buying, downloading, logging in, and waiting. At typical repair rates, that adds up to $12 billion. A separate report from the PIRG Education Fund claims that a two-tiered repair model now exists, where independent sites conduct repairs with less information, less powerful diagnostic tools, and higher associated costs than the authorized dealerships. The advocacy group wants to see legislators take this issue in hand, and has a number of recommendations for them. One is to stop manufacturers from locking out independent mechanics from simple repair jobs like changing brake pads, and require them to support a standard protocol for authenticating independent diagnostic tools. Another is to give owners control over their vehicle’s data via a standardized platform for accessing telematics repair information, so that the owner can give access to an independent repair shop. Car firms can use the vehicle data to tell owners that a repair is needed and to take it to an approved repair shop, without even disclosing what the issue is. DIY repairers should be able to get everything they need to fix their own cars. science.title: Watch live on Nov. 23: Amazon launching 1st batch of internet satellites since Vulcan Centaur failure
science.description: null Another batch of Amazon internet satellites will fly on Monday morning (Nov. 23), just eight days after a launch failure doomed 40 of the spacecraft. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation is scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana on Monday, during a 29-minute window that opens at 6:09 a.m. EST (1109 GMT; 8:09 a.m. local time in Kourou). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of Arianespace, the French company that operates the Ariane 6. Coverage will begin about 30 minutes before launch. An Ariane 6 rocket launches 32 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit from French Guiana on Feb. 12, 2026. (Image credit: ESA/CNES/Arianespace-ArianeGroup/Optique Video du CSG-P. Piron) Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit , will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur , suffered a problem shortly after launch. Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9 . Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test. The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure. Monday's mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year.

science.title: 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson
science.description: 7 Min Read 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano, former NASA astronaut Russell “Rusty” Schweickart, and NASA astronauts Frank Rubio and Bob Hines appear onstage at the Artemis Celebration Gala at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida, on Nov. 6, 2026. Credits: Purpose Entertainment/Shanna Lockwood Employees and guests of NASA’s Johnson Space Center celebrate the center’s 65th anniversary at the Lunar Receiving Park in Houston on Nov. 19, 2026. NASA/Robert Markowitz For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and systems for NASA’s next chapter: returning astronauts to the lunar surface and building the capabilities needed for a long-term human presence at the Moon. Across those missions, generations of flight controllers, engineers, scientists, instructors, medical specialists, and other experts have helped crews live and work beyond Earth. Johnson is home to NASA’s Orion and Moon Base programs, and its teams continue to support space station operations, astronaut training, spacecraft development, mission operations, and human health. Mercury and Gemini: Preparing for Apollo When the Manned Spacecraft Center officially opened on Nov. 1, 1961, NASA had already flown two suborbital Mercury missions, with the first orbital flight just months away. Most Project Mercury activities remained at Cape Canaveral in Florida to maintain continuity, but the new Project Gemini took up residence in Houston, housed in temporary leased facilities across the city while construction of the new Clear Lake campus continued. The new Mission Control Center became NASA’s primary flight control center in June 1965, with the Gemini IV mission that included the first American spacewalk. Houston became the nerve center for American human spaceflight, overseeing the remaining eight Gemini missions before transitioning to the Apollo program. Following the tragic Apollo 1 fire in January 1967, managers, engineers, and astronauts at the Manned Spacecraft Center applied lessons learned to make the spacecraft safer and ensure the safety of its astronauts, resuming crewed missions in October 1968. Managers in Houston devised a daring plan to send Apollo 8 on a circumlunar flight. In December 1968, Apollo 8 made its historic trip around the Moon, and seven months later Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin “Buzz” Aldrin landed on the lunar surface. Their first voice transmission back to Earth after their arrival began with the word “Houston.” Five more Moon landings completed the Apollo program and humanity’s first phase of lunar exploration

science.title: SpaceX sends classified US spy satellites to orbit in early-morning launch from California coast (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched a batch of classified satellites this morning (Nov. 22), on the NROL-136 mission out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California). It was the sixth National Reconnaissance Office launch (NROL) this year to deliver a payload, or group of payloads, to low Earth orbit , all which have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9. The launch marks another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the NROL-136 mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office from California on Nov. 22, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch. Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA 's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the U.S. Space Force , and eight Starlink missions. NROL-136 is the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space , according to the NRO's mission website . The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026. As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
science.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. science.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. Chaos in Luxor How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor.

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). science.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
science.description: null The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. But the company had never attempted a Ship catch, which is a taller order, given how much faster and farther Starship upper stages fly. So snagging Ship on the first try was a very big deal, according to Musk. "Everyone knew, within SpaceX, at least, how important this milestone was, and that it was really something fundamental and profound — that Starship will be the first-ever fully reusable orbital space system," he told Baker and Gracias on Wednesday. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo mission becomes 2nd ever to arrive in orbit around Mercury
science.description: null Update for 2 p.m. ET on Nov. 22: On Sunday afternoon (Nov. 22), the BepiColombo team announced that, while the spacecraft did successfully arrive in orbit around Mercury on Saturday (Nov. 21), things didn't go entirely according to plan. "During the manoeuvre, the thruster burn was shorter than planned due to a software issue," the mission team said via X . "The spacecraft is safe & teams at ESOC are working to understand what happened. Updates provided on Monday." For just the second time ever, Mercury has received a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — arrived in orbit around Mercury on Saturday (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. Before BepiColombo, just one spacecraft had ever circled the solar system's innermost planet: NASA's MESSENGER , which did so from March 2011 to April 2015. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must therefore shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Saturday's orbital insertion came after a 37-minute-long engine burn, which began at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT). There was a bit drama involved, however, as confirmation of the maneuver's success didn't come for several hours afterward. "We've heard back from Bepi — the spacecraft is now in contact with the ground and the teams at ESOC [the European Space Operations Centre] are busy assessing the telemetry. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit. science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. science.description: null On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station. Today, the I nternational Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze. science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

Awards to small businesses around the country are addressing some of NASA’s most crucial technology needs for exploration of the Moon and Mars while fueling the U.S. space economy. NASA’s Small Business Innovation Research/Small Business Technology Transfer (SBIR/STTR) program recently selected 302 innovative projects, for a total investment of up to $171 million in seed funding. This early-stage research and development work will tackle an array of topics, including those related to Artemis and the establishment of a U.S. Moon Base . Selected projects include next-generation battery solutions, robotic systems with sensing capabilities for the extreme lunar environment, and tools to prepare for construction of critical infrastructure, such as lunar landing pads. NASA’s SBIR/STTR program provides support for entrepreneurs, startups, and small businesses to advance and commercialize technologies that can advance the agency’s missions. Working with the program, a company’s path toward commercialization or infusion into NASA missions occurs in phases. The latest awards involved two of these phases. The new Phase I contracts will receive up to $225,000 each to establish the merit and feasibility of their proposed innovation. A portion of the projects selected are STTR awards, provided to small businesses partnered with research institutions. The Phase II awards, with 98 contracts valued at up to $1.3 million each, will continue work begun in Phase I projects selected in 2025, targeting demonstration and delivery of the innovative technologies.
